# TDPdf v1.29.1.0

**Three fixes from the first round of hands-on testing of the 1.29.x tab/window work: an overlapping toolbar, a Text tool that looked broken, and a multi-file open that could quietly stop partway through.**

## Toolbar buttons no longer overlap

At a narrower window width, or a higher UI scale, the toolbar's two button groups could overlap — one group drawing on top of the other wherever their natural widths collided. The group in constant use (the editing tools and zoom controls) now always keeps its full width; the file-operations group gets whatever space is left and scrolls horizontally instead, the same way the tab strip already handles overflow.

## Placed text can be moved and resized right away

Adding a text annotation used to drop it exactly where clicked with no way to nudge it afterward short of knowing to switch to the Select tool first — and once committed, the box had no visible border to even suggest that was needed. If it landed on top of existing content, there was no way to fix that. Text placement now auto-selects the new annotation immediately, the same way placing an image or a signature already does.

## Opening several files at once is more resilient

File → Open with multiple files selected, or dropping several files at once, ran each file through the same code path with no isolation between them — if one file failed partway through, every file after it in the selection went unattempted, with nothing said about why fewer tabs appeared than expected. Each file's open now stands on its own; a failure is reported and the rest of the batch still opens.

## Also confirmed, nothing to fix

- **Rotate** was never a toolbar button — it's on the right-click menu for a page thumbnail in the Pages panel.
- **Taskbar showing only one live preview across multiple TDPdf windows** has an existing answer: **Settings → "Use native window frame."** The default custom title bar renders as a layered window, which is a known case where Windows can't generate a separate live thumbnail per window; the native frame option turns that off.
